newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to interview North Korea defector.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to interview North Korea defector.

text.p: The United States will interview an important defector from North Korea to find out if that country's leaders plan to go to war, Defence Secretary William Cohen said on Sunday.
"It is one of the most dangerous flashpoints in the world," Cohen said on NBC Television's "Meet the Press" programme when asked if North Korea was intent on war.
He said South Korea has agreed to give the United States a chance to interrogate the defector, Hwang Jang-yop, the highest-ranked North Korean ever to flee his communist homeland.
Cohen said that on his recent trip to South Korea officials agreed "the United States will have access to this defector to find out what is in the hearts and minds of the Korean leadership."
Hwang, who arrived in South Korea on Sunday after a stay in the Phillipines, said in a statement: "North Korea seems to think there is no option but to use the forces they have amassed."

"The North Korean economy is almost paralysed. People are suffering from starvation and the government has no choice but to beg from international agencies," he added in the statement read to reporters and broadcast live on television.
It was the first public glimpse of Hwang since he walked into a South Korean embassy compound in Beijing.

The chief architect of North Korea's guiding ideology of "juche", or self-reliance, he is a former confidante of leader Kim Jong-il and holds the innermost secrets of the world's most tightly-sealed society.
Cohen did not spell out when or how U.S. officials would get to see Hwang.
